issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and final order
issues.why: The court must confirm the May 12, 2025 judgment is a final appealable order and that the appeal is properly before it.

issues.label: Timeliness of appeal
issues.why: The court must determine whether the notice of appeal was filed within App.R. 4 time limits or whether any exception applies.

issues.label: Mootness after guilty plea
issues.why: The court must decide which claims survive a guilty plea and which are waived except for jurisdictional defects.

issues.label: Proper standard of review
issues.why: The court must select the correct standards (R.C. 2953.08(G)(2), abuse of discretion, plain error, Strickland) for each claim.

issues.label: Preservation of sentencing error
issues.why: The court must determine whether Arrington objected at sentencing and whether plain-error review under Crim.R. 52(B) applies.

issues.label: Record adequacy for review
issues.why: The court must ensure the record includes the sentencing transcript, PSI information if any, and documents needed to assess compliance and prejudice.

issues.label: Scope of R.C. 2953.08 review
issues.why: The court must decide whether the claimed error fits within R.C. 2953.08(A) and how R.C. 2953.08(G) limits relief.

issues.label: Sentence within statutory range
issues.why: The court must verify the imposed indefinite term is authorized for a second-degree felony under the Reagan Tokes scheme and related statutes.

issues.label: Reagan Tokes applicability
issues.why: The court must determine whether R.C. 2967.271 applies to this offense/date and whether the minimum/maximum calculation is correct.

issues.label: Youthful offender sentencing statute applies
issues.why: The court must decide whether R.C. 2929.19(B)(1)(b) applies to a juvenile-bindover defendant sentenced in adult court.

issues.label: Definition of 'child' at sentencing
issues.why: The court must determine whether Arrington qualifies as a 'child' for purposes of R.C. 2929.19(B)(1)(b) when sentenced (age/status after transfer).

issues.label: Mandatory nature of youth consideration
issues.why: The court must decide whether R.C. 2929.19(B)(1)(b) creates mandatory findings/consideration and what constitutes compliance on the record.

issues.label: What must be 'considered'
issues.why: The court must identify the required youth-related factors and whether the court must address 'attendant characteristics' explicitly or implicitly.

issues.label: Required record articulation
issues.why: The court must decide whether the trial court must state on the record that it considered youth and its attendant characteristics or whether silence can suffice.

issues.label: Use of prior amenability evidence
issues.why: The court must determine whether the juvenile-court psychological/amenability material was before the sentencing court and could satisfy youth-factor consideration.

issues.label: PSI requirement or waiver
issues.why: The court must assess whether a PSI was required, requested, waived, or substituted, and whether its absence affects youth-factor consideration.

issues.label: Opportunity to present mitigation
issues.why: The court must decide whether Arrington had a meaningful chance to present youth mitigation at sentencing, including allocution and counsel argument.

issues.label: Immediate sentencing after plea
issues.why: The court must assess whether proceeding directly from plea to sentencing affected statutory compliance or due process (e.g., time to gather mitigation).

issues.label: Crim.R. 11 plea validity
issues.why: If implicated, the court must ensure the guilty plea was knowing, intelligent, and voluntary, because plea validity can affect waiver and remedy.

issues.label: Effect of guilty plea on sentencing claims
issues.why: The court must determine whether a guilty plea waives statutory-sentencing-procedure errors or whether such errors remain reviewable.

issues.label: Ohio Const. Art. I §9 relevance
issues.why: The court must decide whether Article I, §9 provides an independent state-constitutional basis requiring youth consideration or affects the remedy.

issues.label: State v. Patrick interpretation
issues.why: The court must determine what Patrick requires (record statements, factor analysis, harmlessness) and whether it controls in this district.

issues.label: Harmless error vs structural error
issues.why: The court must decide whether failure to comply with R.C. 2929.19(B)(1)(b) is reversible per se or subject to harmless-error analysis.

issues.label: Plain-error prejudice showing
issues.why: If plain error applies, the court must decide whether the error affected the outcome—i.e., a reasonable probability of a different sentence.

issues.label: Sentencing statutes generally complied
issues.why: The court must confirm compliance with R.C. 2929.11 and 2929.12 and any other mandatory advisements, as they may intersect with youth consideration.

issues.label: Consecutive-sentence issues
issues.why: The court must confirm no consecutive-sentence findings were required or omitted (even if not raised) and whether any were imposed.

issues.label: Postrelease control advisement
issues.why: The court must verify proper imposition and notification of postrelease control obligations for the felony level.

issues.label: Credit for time served
issues.why: The court must ensure jail-time credit was addressed correctly, including time in DYS/custody after transfer, if applicable.

issues.label: Victim-related statutory considerations
issues.why: The court must ensure any required victim-notification, restitution, or rights issues were addressed where applicable.

issues.label: Competency at plea/sentencing
issues.why: Given noted mental-health issues, the court must consider whether there was reason to doubt competency and whether the court should have held a competency evaluation.

issues.label: Voluntariness of waiver at bindover
issues.why: Although not directly appealed, the court must consider whether any jurisdictional defect in transfer exists that could undermine adult-court authority.

issues.label: Bindover statutory compliance
issues.why: The court must ensure the transfer complied with R.C. 2152.10 and 2151.12 (probable cause, amenability procedures), as defects can affect jurisdiction.

issues.label: Validity of probable-cause stipulation
issues.why: The court must consider whether the juvenile probable-cause waiver/stipulation was knowing and voluntary under required safeguards.

issues.label: Right to counsel and GAL in juvenile court
issues.why: The court must confirm juvenile proceedings included required representation and protections, because absence may invalidate transfer.

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction after transfer
issues.why: The court must decide whether the General Division properly acquired jurisdiction via a valid bindover and subsequent indictment.

issues.label: Indictment validity and sufficiency
issues.why: The court must confirm the indictment properly charged felonious assault with correct elements/degree and did not create sentencing exposure errors.

issues.label: Allied offense/merger issues
issues.why: The court must consider whether any merger issues exist (even if single count) and whether sentencing reflected correct offense conduct.

issues.label: IAC standard (Strickland)
issues.why: The court must apply deficient-performance and prejudice standards to counsel’s alleged failure to present youth mitigation.

issues.label: IAC record-based vs extra-record
issues.why: The court must decide whether the ineffectiveness claim is resolvable on direct appeal or requires postconviction evidence outside the record.

issues.label: Counsel duty to investigate mitigation
issues.why: The court must assess whether counsel had a duty to obtain/present youth and mental-health mitigation (including the Feb. 3, 2025 evaluation).

issues.label: Counsel strategic choice vs deficiency
issues.why: The court must determine whether not presenting youth factors was a reasonable tactical decision or fell below professional norms.

issues.label: Prejudice from missing mitigation
issues.why: The court must decide whether there is a reasonable probability the sentencing court would have imposed a shorter minimum term or different disposition with youth evidence.

issues.label: Link between IAC and statutory error
issues.why: The court must assess whether counsel’s omission caused the R.C. 2929.19(B)(1)(b) noncompliance and whether that strengthens prejudice/relief.

issues.label: Sentencing court’s consideration absent counsel
issues.why: The court must determine whether the judge independently considered youth factors despite counsel’s silence, which could defeat prejudice.

issues.label: Remedy for statutory noncompliance
issues.why: If error is found, the court must decide the proper remedy (resentencing hearing, new sentencing entry, or limited remand) and scope of proceedings.

issues.label: Remedy for ineffective assistance
issues.why: If IAC is found, the court must decide whether to vacate sentence only, or plea and sentence, and what proceedings are required on remand.

issues.label: Resentencing de novo scope
issues.why: The court must determine whether resentencing is de novo (allowing new evidence) and whether the same judge must conduct it.

issues.label: Use of youth evaluation on remand
issues.why: The court must decide whether the psychological evaluation must be introduced, whether it is admissible, and how it should be considered at resentencing.

issues.label: Confidentiality of juvenile records
issues.why: The court must consider restrictions on juvenile-court records/psych reports and how they may be used in adult sentencing.

issues.label: Due process at sentencing
issues.why: The court must ensure the sentence was imposed after procedures satisfying due process, including reliable information and an opportunity to rebut.

issues.label: Equal protection or proportionality
issues.why: The court must consider any proportionality concerns implicated by sentencing a transferred juvenile to adult prison without youth consideration.

issues.label: Eighth Amendment youth principles
issues.why: The court must consider whether constitutional juvenile-sentencing principles (youth culpability) inform interpretation of R.C. 2929.19(B)(1)(b) and the sentence’s legality.

issues.label: Maximum-term selection rationale
issues.why: The court must verify the maximum term (10.5 years) was calculated and imposed as required by the indefinite sentencing statutes.

issues.label: Sentencing entry completeness
issues.why: The court must ensure the judgment entry includes all mandatory components (conviction, sentence, PRC, credits if required) for enforceability and review.
